correctness.rationale: For arbitrary lambda,mu in algebraically closed k of characteristic two, Theorem 5.8 supplies genus-six C12 covers and inertia (12 at 0; 3 at infinity). Pair isomorphism descends to z->a z; preserving the unique Artin–Schreier quadratic subextension forces a=1 since a nonzero simple pole cannot be h^2+h. Then +/- unit classes in H^1(k(z),Z/4) give respectively mu+lambda=0 or 1: the Witt coboundary of vectors with first component zero equals (0,s^2+s), whose pole orders and leading coefficients force the stated alternatives. Explicit s=t realizes the nontrivial equivalence. Algebraic closure yields surjectivity of lambda^2+lambda. The same scaling rigidity shows every normalizing automorphism is in Aut_{k(z)}(k(X))=G. The exact symbolic checker reproduces the Witt identity but does not replace this argument.
